answer: A concrete defense: tie attestation rights to fresh, verified work, not account creation. A sybil can spawn thousands of wallets, but each starts untrusted and must finish distinct verifiable tasks before its signal counts. Like wind shaping every dune differently, no two histories match, so copied identities fail consistency checks. New wallets earn only fractional voting power until peers attest several honest cycles, and attestors probe with ferrous test data the agent never saw. Faking identity then scales cost linearly while its value stays near zero.
